question: According to the Hawaii CDL manual, what is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A hydraulic lift used only to raise landing gear on the lead trailer
choice_b: A type of glad hand used to connect electrical cords between trailers
choice_c: A braking device installed exclusively on the tractor's drive axle
choice_d: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.1 Converter Dolly

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer height?
choice_a: The trailer must be raised as high as possible before the dolly is positioned
choice_b: Trailer height does not matter as long as the kingpin is centered
choice_c: The trailer must be exactly level with the top of the dolly wheels
choice_d: The trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer and raising the landing gear slightly, how should the driver test the coupling?
choice_a: By driving the rig forward at highway speed
choice_b: By pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_c: By disconnecting the safety chains and observing trailer movement
choice_d: By visually inspecting the tires only
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer before making the visual check.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When making a visual check of the coupling between the dolly and the second trailer, what should the driver look for?
choice_a: That the tractor's fuel gauge reads full
choice_b: That the landing gear is fully lowered
choice_c: That the pintle hook is unlatched
choice_d: That there is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
explanation: The manual specifies checking that there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After the visual check of the fifth wheel coupling is complete, what should the driver connect next?
choice_a: Nothing further is required until the next fuel stop
choice_b: Safety chains, air hoses, and light cords
choice_c: The emergency air line only
choice_d: Only the electrical cord, since the dolly has no brakes
explanation: After making the visual check of the coupling, the manual directs the driver to connect safety chains, air hoses, and light cords.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Once the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer are opened and the landing gear is raised completely, what is the final step to charge the trailer brakes?
choice_a: Drain all air tanks completely
choice_b: Apply the trailer hand valve only, without checking air pressure
choice_c: Push the 'air supply' knob in, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off
choice_d: Pull the 'air supply' knob out and disconnect the emergency line
explanation: The manual states to charge trailer brakes by pushing the 'air supply' knob in and checking for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: What is the first step listed for uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of doubles?
choice_a: Release the dolly brakes immediately
choice_b: Disconnect the electrical cord first
choice_c: Park the rig in a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_d: Raise the landing gear of the second semitrailer fully
explanation: The manual lists parking the rig in a straight line on firm level ground as the first step in uncoupling the rear trailer.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why should the landing gear of the second semitrailer be lowered slightly before releasing the converter dolly fifth wheel latch during uncoupling?
choice_a: To disconnect the safety chains automatically
choice_b: It is not part of the uncoupling procedure
choice_c: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_d: To raise the tractor's fifth wheel
explanation: The manual instructs lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly before proceeding with uncoupling.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: After releasing the converter dolly fifth wheel latch during uncoupling of the rear trailer, what should the driver do?
choice_a: Immediately disconnect the tractor from the first trailer
choice_b: Reverse the tractor to push the dolly further under the trailer
choice_c: Lower the landing gear of the first trailer completely
choice_d: Slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer
explanation: The manual states to slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why should a driver never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: It voids the manufacturer's warranty
choice_c: It will cause the tractor's engine to stall
choice_d: It automatically triggers the emergency brakes on all trailers
explanation: The manual warns that unlocking the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer can cause the dolly tow bar to fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: What is the correct order for coupling a triple-trailer rig according to the manual?
choice_a: Couple all three trailers simultaneously using separate dollies
choice_b: Couple the third trailer to the tractor first, then work backward
choice_c: Couple the second and third trailers together before attaching any trailer to the tractor
choice_d: Couple the tractor to the first trailer using the standard tractor-semitrailer method, then move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles
explanation: The manual describes coupling the tractor to the first trailer using the standard method, then moving the converter dolly into position and coupling using the doubles-coupling method to complete the triples rig.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer is detached first?
choice_a: All three trailers are detached at the same time
choice_b: The third trailer, by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it using the method for uncoupling doubles
choice_c: The middle trailer only, leaving the first and third attached
choice_d: The trailer directly behind the tractor
explanation: The manual states to uncouple the third trailer first by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, before uncoupling the remainder of the rig.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When inspecting the lower fifth wheel on a double or triple rig, where should the locking jaws be positioned on the kingpin?
choice_a: Loosely resting against the kingpin without locking
choice_b: Around the head, not the shank, of the kingpin
choice_c: Around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin
choice_d: It does not matter as long as the jaws are closed
explanation: The manual specifies checking that the locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

question: When inspecting the shut-off valves (service and emergency lines) at the rear of trailers in a double or triple combination, what is the correct position?
choice_a: Rear of front trailers should be OPEN; rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
choice_b: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be CLOSED
choice_c: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be OPEN
choice_d: Rear of front trailers should be CLOSED; rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
explanation: The manual states that the shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

question: During the additional walk-around inspection items for doubles and triples, what should be checked regarding the pintle-eye of the dolly?
choice_a: That it is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s) and that the pintle hook is latched
choice_b: That it is painted a bright color
choice_c: That it is removed before driving
choice_d: That it is lubricated with brake fluid
explanation: The manual instructs verifying the pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s) and making sure the pintle hook is latched.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.2 Additional Things to Check during a Walk-around Inspection

question: When testing the tractor protection valve, at approximately what air pressure range should the trailer air supply control pop out (or move from 'normal' to 'emergency')?
choice_a: Usually within the range of 60 to 80 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 90 to 100 psi
choice_c: Usually within the range of 5 to 10 psi
choice_d: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually within 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: How does the manual describe testing the trailer emergency brakes on a double or triple combination?
choice_a: Disconnect all air lines and observe if the trailer rolls
choice_b: Charge the trailer air brake system, check that the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in 'emergency') and pull gently on the trailer to check the emergency brakes are on
choice_c: Apply the parking brake only and check the fuel gauge
choice_d: Simply listen for air escaping at the front of the tractor
explanation: The manual describes charging the trailer air brake system, checking the trailer rolls freely, then pulling out the trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) or placing it in the emergency position, and pulling gently on the trailer to confirm the emergency brakes engage.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Trailer Emergency Brakes

question: According to the manual, how are trailer service brakes normally controlled during operation, even though they should be tested with the hand valve?
choice_a: They cannot be controlled from the cab at all
choice_b: With the parking brake knob exclusively
choice_c: With the foot pedal, which applies air to the service brakes at all wheels
choice_d: With the converter dolly's spring brake lever
explanation: The manual notes that trailer brakes should be tested with the hand valve (trolley valve), but in normal operation they are controlled with the foot pedal, which applies air to the service brakes at all wheels.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Trailer Service Brakes

question: When checking that air flows to all trailers on a double or triple combination, what should the driver do at the rear of the last trailer to confirm the system is charged?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake and check the odometer
choice_b: Open the emergency line shut-off valve and listen for air escaping
choice_c: Disconnect the electrical cord and observe the lights
choice_d: Remove the spare tire and inspect the mounting
explanation: The manual instructs opening the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer; hearing air escaping shows the entire system is charged.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: If, during the air-flow check, the driver does NOT hear air escaping from both the emergency and service lines at the rear of the last trailer, what should be checked?
choice_a: That the tractor's fuel level is adequate
choice_b: That the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position, since air must reach all the way to the back for all the brakes to work
choice_c: That the safety chains are the correct length
choice_d: Nothing further; this is the expected, normal result
explanation: The manual states that if air is not heard escaping from both lines, the driver should check that the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are OPEN, since air must reach all the way to the back for all the brakes to work.
source_note: Hawaii Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, Hawaii: May 2023), State of Hawaii CDL Program / AAMVA, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Check That Air Flows to All Trailers
